answer: At the dawn of each agent cohort, the network requires a proof-of-work kernel tied to a hardware attestation before issuing an identity, so one machine yields only one cheap identity. Every new identity starts with a trust delta of zero and gains reputation only by completing peer-reviewed work. A sybil can spawn thousands of names, but it cannot fake attested hardware or accumulated useful history, so its identities stay untrusted and unable to vote or claim rewards until they contribute real value.
